title: 计算机科学，从零搭建 · 第11部分：运行中的程序

chapters.Hook: 从文本到运行中的进程
chapters.Allocators: 7. 五个分配器，一条真实轨迹
chapters.Theory: 8. 克努特法则与罗布森界
chapters.Outro: 回顾、习题，以及它们会在哪里再出现

b6bffd61b5a4.en: Until now every Pebble program has been one file of assembly, written by hand, that the machine runs from address zero. Real programs are not like that. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is the Job again, written the way a compiler would write it: four separate files. The main loop; the word table, now a linked list of nodes on a heap; a memory allocator; and the input and output routines. Each is assembled on its own, and each has holes in it: places where it uses a name, like lookup or alloc, whose address it cannot know. <bookmark mark='b'/> A linker fills the holes and joins the four into one program. <bookmark mark='c'/> It prints exactly the same twenty words as Part 6's program, and on the first chapter it is even a little faster.
b6bffd61b5a4.zh: 到目前为止，每个 Pebble 程序都是一个手写的汇编文件，机器从地址零开始运行它。真实的程序不是这样的。<bookmark mark='a'/>这又是任务，按编译器会写的方式写成：四个独立的文件。主循环；单词表，现在是堆上节点组成的链表；一个内存分配器；以及输入输出例程。每个文件单独汇编，每个都留着洞：在那些地方它用到一个名字，比如 lookup 或 alloc，却不可能知道它的地址。<bookmark mark='b'/>链接器把这些洞填上，把四个文件合成一个程序。<bookmark mark='c'/>它打印的二十个词和第6部分的程序一模一样，在第一章上甚至还快一点。

977a742b7d06.en: And here is a program that does something its author never wrote. <bookmark mark='a'/> It asks for a name and says hello, copying the name into a buffer of sixty-four bytes. <bookmark mark='b'/> Give it a name, and it greets you. <bookmark mark='c'/> Give it eighty-one carefully chosen bytes, and it prints pwned, a word that appears nowhere in the program. <bookmark mark='d'/> The input ran past the end of the buffer, overwrote the address the function was going to return to, and the processor returned into the input itself. To see how, and how to stop it, we need to know how a running program is laid out in memory.
977a742b7d06.zh: 这里还有一个程序，它会做作者从没写过的事。<bookmark mark='a'/>它问你的名字，然后打招呼，把名字复制进一个六十四字节的缓冲区。<bookmark mark='b'/>给它一个名字，它就向你问好。<bookmark mark='c'/>给它八十一个精心挑选的字节，它就打印出 pwned，一个程序里根本没有的词。<bookmark mark='d'/>输入越过了缓冲区的末尾，覆盖了函数将要返回的地址，处理器就返回到了输入本身里面。要看懂这是怎么回事、又怎样阻止它，我们得先知道一个运行中的程序在内存里是怎样布局的。

7376514d91fb.en: Here is where this part goes. <bookmark mark='a'/> How a program's data sits in memory: bytes and words, alignment, arrays and pointers. <bookmark mark='b'/> How procedures work: the call stack, its frames, and the conventions that let separately written functions call each other. <bookmark mark='c'/> The heap, with five memory allocators run on a real program's allocations, and the theorems that say how well any allocator can do. <bookmark mark='d'/> Object files, linking and loading, on Pebble and on this computer. <bookmark mark='e'/> And what goes wrong: undefined behaviour, and the stack smash, with the defences every program now ships with.
7376514d91fb.zh: 这一部分要去的地方是这样的。<bookmark mark='a'/>程序的数据怎样待在内存里：字节和字、对齐、数组和指针。<bookmark mark='b'/>过程是怎样工作的：调用栈、栈帧，以及让分别编写的函数能互相调用的约定。<bookmark mark='c'/>堆：五个内存分配器跑在一个真实程序的分配序列上，以及说明任何分配器能做到多好的定理。<bookmark mark='d'/>目标文件、链接和装载，在 Pebble 上，也在这台计算机上。<bookmark mark='e'/>还有会出的错：未定义行为，以及栈溢出攻击，连同如今每个程序都自带的防御。

0c428451993d.en: This is Part 11 of Computer Science, Built, and the first part of Act Three, Speaking to the Machine. <bookmark mark='a'/> In this part: a program's life from source to process. Bytes, endianness and alignment, and control flow as machine code. The call stack, calling conventions, recursion and tail calls. The heap and its allocators, with Knuth's fifty-percent rule and Robson's bound. Object files, static and dynamic linking, and the address space. Undefined behaviour, the stack smash, and the Job, linked from four files.
0c428451993d.zh: 这是《计算机科学，从零搭建》的第11部分，第三幕“和机器对话”的第一部分。<bookmark mark='a'/>这一部分讲：程序从源代码到进程的一生。字节、字节序和对齐，以及机器码里的控制流。调用栈、调用约定、递归和尾调用。堆和它的分配器，以及克努特的五十百分比法则和罗布森界。目标文件、静态和动态链接，以及地址空间。未定义行为、栈溢出攻击，以及由四个文件链接起来的任务。

bf3a8f6687d1.en: A program goes through five hands on its way to running. <bookmark mark='a'/> It starts as source code, text that a person wrote. <bookmark mark='b'/> A compiler translates it into assembly language; Part 13 builds one. <bookmark mark='c'/> An assembler, which Part 6 built, turns the assembly into machine words, but it works on one file at a time, so wherever the file uses a name defined somewhere else it must leave a hole, and a note saying what goes there. That is an object file. <bookmark mark='d'/> The linker reads all the object files, decides where everything goes, and fills every hole. <bookmark mark='e'/> Finally the operating system's loader copies the program into memory, sets up a stack with the program's arguments, and jumps to its first instruction. Now it is a process.
bf3a8f6687d1.zh: 一个程序在运行之前要经过五双手。<bookmark mark='a'/>它从源代码开始，一段人写的文本。<bookmark mark='b'/>编译器把它翻译成汇编语言；第13部分会搭一个。<bookmark mark='c'/>汇编器，第6部分搭过，把汇编变成机器字，但它一次只处理一个文件，所以只要文件用到别处定义的名字，它就得留一个洞，外加一张条子说明那里该填什么。这就是目标文件。<bookmark mark='d'/>链接器读入所有目标文件，决定每样东西放在哪里，并把每个洞填上。<bookmark mark='e'/>最后，操作系统的装载器把程序复制进内存，建好带着程序参数的栈，跳到它的第一条指令。现在它是一个进程了。

6f464e7a7553.en: Follow one call through. <bookmark mark='a'/> In the source it is a call to lookup, with the word and its length. <bookmark mark='b'/> In assembly it becomes call lookup. <bookmark mark='c'/> But lookup is in another file, so the assembler cannot know how far away it is. It emits a jump-and-link with an offset of zero, <bookmark mark='d'/> and a note, a relocation: at byte eighty-eight of my code, put the distance to lookup, in the 22-bit form a jump uses. <bookmark mark='e'/> The linker places main's code at address zero and the table's code after it, so lookup lands at 144. It writes the distance, 14 instructions, into the hole. Nothing else about the word changes.
6f464e7a7553.zh: 跟着一次调用走一遍。<bookmark mark='a'/>在源代码里，它是对 lookup 的一次调用，带着词和它的长度。<bookmark mark='b'/>在汇编里，它变成 call lookup。<bookmark mark='c'/>但 lookup 在另一个文件里，所以汇编器不可能知道它有多远。它发出一条偏移为零的跳转并链接，<bookmark mark='d'/>外加一张条子，一条重定位：在我的代码第八十八个字节处，填上到 lookup 的距离，用跳转所用的 22 位形式。<bookmark mark='e'/>链接器把 main 的代码放在地址零，把表的代码放在它后面，于是 lookup 落在 144。它把距离，14 条指令，写进那个洞。这个字的其余部分什么都没变。

f6bda8d1153d.en: Memory is a row of bytes, but most values are bigger than a byte. <bookmark mark='a'/> A 32-bit word takes four of them, and someone has to decide their order. <bookmark mark='b'/> Big-endian machines store the most significant byte first, the way we write numbers; network protocols do the same. <bookmark mark='c'/> Little-endian machines store the least significant byte first. x86, Arm in its usual mode, RISC-V and Pebble are all little-endian, and this computer confirms it: the four bytes of zero A zero B zero C zero D sit in memory as zero D, zero C, zero B, zero A. <bookmark mark='d'/> The names come from a 1980 memo by Danny Cohen, after the war in Gulliver's Travels over which end of an egg to break. Neither order is better; mixing them up is a classic bug whenever bytes cross a network or a file.
f6bda8d1153d.zh: 内存是一排字节，但大多数值都比一个字节大。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个 32 位的字要占四个字节，总得有人决定它们的次序。<bookmark mark='b'/>大端机器把最高位的字节放在前面，就像我们写数字那样；网络协议也这么做。<bookmark mark='c'/>小端机器把最低位的字节放在前面。x86、通常模式下的 Arm、RISC-V 和 Pebble 都是小端，这台计算机证实了这一点：0A 0B 0C 0D 这四个字节在内存里依次是 0D、0C、0B、0A。<bookmark mark='d'/>这两个名字来自丹尼·科恩 1980 年的一份备忘录，取自《格列佛游记》里为该从哪一头敲开鸡蛋而打的仗。两种次序没有哪个更好；字节跨越网络或文件时把它们弄混，是一个经典的错误。

136a87965cfb.en: Values also have to sit at sensible addresses. <bookmark mark='a'/> A four-byte integer normally lives at an address divisible by four, so that it never straddles two cache lines and can be fetched in one transfer; Pebble's own loads demand it. <bookmark mark='b'/> So a compiler pads structures. A character, an integer and a character take six bytes of data, but laid out in that order they take 12: three bytes of padding after the first character so the integer is aligned, and three at the end so that an array of these stays aligned too. <bookmark mark='c'/> Put the largest field first and the same data fits in 8. <bookmark mark='d'/> The Job's list node, two pointers and two integers, is 24 bytes on this 64-bit machine and sixteen on Pebble, where a pointer is four bytes. These sizes were measured here, by compiling the structures and asking.
136a87965cfb.zh: 值还得放在合适的地址上。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个四字节的整数通常放在能被四整除的地址上，这样它就不会横跨两个缓存行，一次传输就能取到；Pebble 自己的取数就要求这样。<bookmark mark='b'/>所以编译器会给结构体加填充。一个字符、一个整数、一个字符，数据只有六个字节，但按这个次序排就要占12个：第一个字符后面三个字节的填充，让整数对齐；末尾再三个，让这种结构体组成的数组也保持对齐。<bookmark mark='c'/>把最大的字段放在最前面，同样的数据装进8个字节。<bookmark mark='d'/>任务的链表节点，两个指针和两个整数，在这台 64 位机器上是24个字节，在指针只有四个字节的 Pebble 上是十六个。这些大小都是在这里测出来的：把结构体编译出来，再问它们。

15daa3362077.en: Arrays are the simplest structure of all. <bookmark mark='a'/> A two-dimensional array of three rows and four columns <bookmark mark='b'/> is stored as one row after another, row-major order, in C and in most languages; Fortran stores columns instead. <bookmark mark='c'/> So the address of element i, j is the start of the array plus four bytes times four i plus j. <bookmark mark='d'/> A pointer is just an address, and adding one to a pointer adds the size of the thing it points to. Indexing an array is pointer arithmetic: a of i means the contents of a plus i. And nothing in the hardware checks that i is inside the array. Chapter fourteen shows what that costs.
15daa3362077.zh: 数组是最简单的结构。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个三行四列的二维数组<bookmark mark='b'/>一行接一行地存放，也就是行主序，在 C 和大多数语言里都是这样；Fortran 则按列存。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以元素 i、j 的地址，是数组的起点加上四个字节乘以四 i 加 j。<bookmark mark='d'/>指针只是一个地址，给指针加一，加的是它所指对象的大小。数组下标就是指针运算：a 的第 i 项意思是 a 加 i 处的内容。而硬件里没有任何东西检查 i 是否在数组之内。第十四章会展示这要付出什么。

619a9e122653.en: Chapter three. Control flow in machine code.
619a9e122653.zh: 第三章。机器码里的控制流。

a7136cf78b78.en: Structured control flow disappears in machine code: everything becomes a branch. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here are two pieces of the Job, in C-like source on the left and Pebble on the right. <bookmark mark='b'/> An if becomes a conditional branch around its body. And notice the trick for the range test: subtract A, and then one unsigned comparison against 26 asks both questions at once, because anything below A wraps round to a huge unsigned number. Compilers do this routinely. <bookmark mark='c'/> A loop becomes a test at the top that leaves, and a jump back at the bottom.
a7136cf78b78.zh: 结构化的控制流在机器码里消失了：一切都变成分支。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是任务的两段，左边是类 C 的源代码，右边是 Pebble。<bookmark mark='b'/>if 变成绕过它主体的条件分支。注意那个范围测试的技巧：先减去 A，然后一次与 26 的无符号比较同时回答两个问题，因为任何小于 A 的值都会绕回成一个巨大的无符号数。编译器经常这样做。<bookmark mark='c'/>循环变成顶部一个决定是否离开的测试，加上底部一个跳回去的跳转。

5e529017c006.en: A switch statement with dense cases gets something better than a chain of ifs. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is a switch with eight cases, compiled on this computer by gcc with optimization. <bookmark mark='b'/> First a single bounds check: is c between zero and seven? <bookmark mark='c'/> Then it loads entry c from a table that the compiler wrote into read-only data, <bookmark mark='d'/> and jumps to the address the entry gives. Whatever the case, two loads and one indirect jump: a jump table. <bookmark mark='e'/> And look at the cases themselves. Each ends with a plain jump to its function, not a call: because nothing is left to do afterwards, the compiler lets that function return directly to our caller. That is a tail call, and chapter five comes back to it.
5e529017c006.zh: 分支密集的 switch 语句会得到比一串 if 更好的东西。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是一个有八个分支的 switch，在这台计算机上用 gcc 开优化编译。<bookmark mark='b'/>先是一次边界检查：c 在零和七之间吗？<bookmark mark='c'/>然后它从编译器写在只读数据里的一张表中取出第 c 项，<bookmark mark='d'/>跳到那一项给出的地址。不管哪个分支，都是两次取数加一次间接跳转：一张跳转表。<bookmark mark='e'/>再看各个分支本身。每个都以一条跳到自己函数的普通跳转结束，而不是调用：因为之后没有别的事要做，编译器就让那个函数直接返回到我们的调用者。这就是尾调用，第五章还会回到它。

a27cfce22ca0.en: For functions written separately, perhaps by different people with different compilers, to call each other, they must agree on the rules: a calling convention. Here is Pebble's. <bookmark mark='a'/> Arguments go in a0 to a5, and the result comes back in a0. The call instruction puts the return address in ra. <bookmark mark='b'/> The registers are split in two. t0 to t3 are temporaries: a function may destroy them, so a caller that needs one after a call must save it itself. s0 to s2 are the opposite: a function that wants to use one must save the old value and restore it before returning, so callers can rely on them. And the stack pointer stays aligned to sixteen bytes. <bookmark mark='c'/> None of this is enforced by the hardware. It is a contract, and real systems write theirs down: the System V application binary interface for Linux and macOS, Microsoft's for Windows, the RISC-V psABI.
a27cfce22ca0.zh: 分别编写的函数，也许出自不同的人、不同的编译器，要互相调用，就必须约定规则：调用约定。这是 Pebble 的。<bookmark mark='a'/>参数放在 a0 到 a5，结果从 a0 带回。call 指令把返回地址放进 ra。<bookmark mark='b'/>寄存器分成两类。t0 到 t3 是临时寄存器：函数可以破坏它们，所以调用之后还需要某个的调用者得自己保存。s0 到 s2 正好相反：想用其中一个的函数，必须先保存旧值，返回前恢复，这样调用者就能依赖它们。栈指针始终按十六字节对齐。<bookmark mark='c'/>这些都不是硬件强制的。它是一份契约，真实的系统都把它写下来：Linux 和 macOS 的 System V 应用二进制接口，Windows 的微软接口，RISC-V 的 psABI。

0a6eef013b9e.en: Here is what a function does with that contract. <bookmark mark='a'/> lookup will use s0, s1 and s2, and it calls alloc, which overwrites ra. So on entry it moves the stack pointer down sixteen bytes and saves all four there. That block is its stack frame, or activation record. <bookmark mark='b'/> Above it sits the frame of the function that called it, main, holding main's word buffer. <bookmark mark='c'/> On the way out, lookup restores the four registers, moves the stack pointer back up, and returns. Every call pushes a frame and every return pops one, so the stack always mirrors the chain of calls in progress.
0a6eef013b9e.zh: 这是一个函数按这份契约做的事。<bookmark mark='a'/>lookup 会用到 s0、s1 和 s2，而且它会调用 alloc，后者会覆盖 ra。所以一进来它就把栈指针往下移十六个字节，把这四个都存在那里。这一块就是它的栈帧，也叫活动记录。<bookmark mark='b'/>它上面是调用它的函数 main 的栈帧，装着 main 的单词缓冲区。<bookmark mark='c'/>出去的时候，lookup 恢复这四个寄存器，把栈指针移回去，然后返回。每次调用压入一个帧，每次返回弹出一个，所以栈总是映照着正在进行的那一串调用。

1458acf1f2a6.en: Watch it on a recursive function, the factorial. <bookmark mark='a'/> fact of ten calls fact of nine, which calls fact of eight, and so on down to one, each call pushing a frame holding its own n and its return address. <bookmark mark='b'/> Here is the stack's depth, measured on Pebble's emulator instruction by instruction: it climbs to ten frames, then, as each call returns and multiplies, it unwinds to nothing. <bookmark mark='c'/> The result is ten factorial, and the deepest the stack went was a hundred and sixty bytes.
1458acf1f2a6.zh: 在一个递归函数上看看，阶乘。<bookmark mark='a'/>fact(10) 调用 fact(9)，后者调用 fact(8)，一直到一，每次调用压入一个帧，装着它自己的 n 和返回地址。<bookmark mark='b'/>这是在 Pebble 模拟器上逐条指令测出的栈深度：它爬升到十个帧，然后随着每次调用返回并相乘，退回到零。<bookmark mark='c'/>结果是十的阶乘，栈最深时是一百六十个字节。

c3286285c209.en: A debugger reads the same structure on a real machine. <bookmark mark='a'/> We compiled a C factorial on this computer, ran it under gdb, and stopped it at its deepest call, fact of one. <bookmark mark='b'/> Asked for a backtrace, gdb lists six frames: five calls of fact and main. <bookmark mark='c'/> It finds them by walking the stack. Each frame keeps its caller's frame address and its own return address, so from the stack pointer the debugger can step from frame to frame. The stack pointers it reports are thirty-two bytes apart, one frame of fact each. <bookmark mark='d'/> And the saved return addresses tell the story of the calls: four of them point to the same instruction in fact, the one just after the recursive call; the fifth returns into main, and main's into the C library that started it. That is all a backtrace is.
c3286285c209.zh: 调试器在真实的机器上读的是同一个结构。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们在这台计算机上编译了一个 C 写的阶乘，在 gdb 里运行，让它停在最深的那次调用，fact(1)。<bookmark mark='b'/>要它给出回溯，gdb 列出六个栈帧：五次 fact 调用和 main。<bookmark mark='c'/>它是沿着栈走过去找到它们的。每个栈帧都保存着调用者的帧地址和自己的返回地址，所以调试器从栈指针出发，就能一帧一帧地走。它报告的栈指针彼此相差三十二个字节，每个是 fact 的一个栈帧。<bookmark mark='d'/>保存的返回地址讲出了这串调用的故事：其中四个指向 fact 里的同一条指令，也就是递归调用之后的那一条；第五个返回进 main，而 main 的返回进启动它的 C 库。回溯不过如此。

e230aa3ee6f1.en: Chapter five. Recursion, depth, and tail calls.
e230aa3ee6f1.zh: 第五章。递归、深度与尾调用。

05b3aa2abfd6.en: Recursion can make the stack enormous. <bookmark mark='a'/> Wilhelm Ackermann's function, from 1928, is defined by three short rules, and Part 25 explains why it matters: it is computable, but it grows faster than anything a fixed number of loops can compute. <bookmark mark='b'/> We ran it on Pebble. A of three, six is just five hundred and nine, but computing it takes a hundred and seventy-two thousand calls, and at its deepest the stack holds five hundred and eleven frames. Each step up in n roughly quadruples the calls and doubles the depth. <bookmark mark='c'/> A of four, two has nearly twenty thousand digits. Recursion like this is limited not by time alone but by the stack.
05b3aa2abfd6.zh: 递归可以让栈变得巨大。<bookmark mark='a'/>威廉·阿克曼 1928 年的函数由三条短规则定义，第25部分会解释它为什么重要：它是可计算的，但增长得比任何固定层数的循环能算出的东西都快。<bookmark mark='b'/>我们在 Pebble 上运行了它。A(3, 6) 只是五百零九，但算它要调用十七万两千次，最深时栈上有五百一十一个帧。n 每增加一，调用次数大约变成四倍，深度翻倍。<bookmark mark='c'/>A(4, 2) 有将近两万位数字。这样的递归不只受时间限制，也受栈的限制。

367e79220f9e.en: Some recursion can be made free. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here the recursive call is the very last thing the function does; its result is returned unchanged. That is a tail call. <bookmark mark='b'/> There is then no reason to come back: the frame holds nothing anyone needs. So instead of calling, the function can simply jump to itself, and when the innermost one returns, it returns straight to the original caller. <bookmark mark='c'/> On Pebble, summing a hundred numbers the first way uses 1,616 bytes of stack and 1,013 instructions; the second, no stack at all and less than half the instructions. Scheme requires this optimization; C compilers do it when they can, as the jump table of the last chapter showed; Python, deliberately, never does.
367e79220f9e.zh: 有些递归可以变得免费。<bookmark mark='a'/>这里递归调用是函数做的最后一件事；它的结果原样返回。这就是尾调用。<bookmark mark='b'/>那么就没有理由再回来：这个帧里没有谁需要的东西。所以函数不必调用，直接跳到自己就行，最里面那一层返回时，它直接返回到最初的调用者。<bookmark mark='c'/>在 Pebble 上，用第一种办法把一百个数加起来，要用1616字节的栈和1013条指令；第二种完全不用栈，指令也不到一半。Scheme 要求这种优化；C 编译器能做时就做，正如上一章的跳转表所示；Python 则有意从不这样做。

7154129f2f74.en: What happens when the stack runs out? <bookmark mark='a'/> A thread's stack has a fixed size, chosen when it starts: eight megabytes by default on Linux, one on Windows. <bookmark mark='b'/> Below it the operating system leaves a guard page that is not mapped at all, so running past the end is caught as a segmentation fault rather than silently trampling other memory. <bookmark mark='c'/> Languages with their own runtimes catch it earlier: Python stops at a thousand frames, Java throws a stack overflow error. <bookmark mark='d'/> Two functions calling each other count just as much as one calling itself. <bookmark mark='e'/> The cure for deep recursion is to keep the pending work in an explicit stack on the heap, or to turn it into a loop.
7154129f2f74.zh: 栈用完了会怎样？<bookmark mark='a'/>一个线程的栈大小是固定的，在它启动时就选好：Linux 上默认八兆字节，Windows 上一兆。<bookmark mark='b'/>在它下面，操作系统留了一个根本没有映射的保护页，所以越过末尾会被当作段错误抓住，而不是悄悄践踏别的内存。<bookmark mark='c'/>有自己运行时的语言会更早抓住它：Python 在一千个帧时停下，Java 抛出栈溢出错误。<bookmark mark='d'/>两个函数互相调用，和一个函数调用自己一样算数。<bookmark mark='e'/>深递归的药方，是把待做的工作放进堆上一个显式的栈里，或者把它改成循环。

5bcbe05930ec.en: The stack is perfect for data that lives exactly as long as a function call. <bookmark mark='a'/> But much data is not like that. <bookmark mark='b'/> The Job's table outlives every call that adds to it, and nobody knows in advance how big it will grow. <bookmark mark='c'/> For that there is the heap: ask malloc for n bytes, and you get a pointer to them, valid until you hand them back with free. <bookmark mark='d'/> Behind those two functions is a hard problem. Requests arrive in any order and any size. The allocator must decide where each one goes at once, without knowing the future, and once it has handed out an address it can never move the block, because the program holds pointers to it.
5bcbe05930ec.zh: 栈非常适合那些寿命恰好和一次函数调用一样长的数据。<bookmark mark='a'/>但很多数据不是这样。<bookmark mark='b'/>任务的表比每一个往里添东西的调用都活得长，而且没人事先知道它会长多大。<bookmark mark='c'/>为此有了堆：向 malloc 要 n 个字节，你会得到一个指向它们的指针，一直有效，直到你用 free 把它们交还。<bookmark mark='d'/>这两个函数背后是一个难题。请求以任意次序、任意大小到来。分配器必须立刻决定每一个放在哪里，却不知道将来，而且一旦交出了地址，就再也不能移动这个块，因为程序握着指向它的指针。

f05926f0492b.en: Here is the classic design. <bookmark mark='a'/> The heap is one stretch of memory cut into blocks, each starting with a small header that records its size and whether it is in use. <bookmark mark='b'/> The free blocks are linked together into a list. <bookmark mark='c'/> To allocate, walk the list for a block that is big enough, hand out the front of it, and leave the rest on the list. <bookmark mark='d'/> To free, mark the block free, and if its neighbours are free too, merge them into one larger block, so that the heap does not crumble into pieces too small to use. <bookmark mark='e'/> Finding the next neighbour is easy, since its header follows ours. Finding the previous one is the clever part: Donald Knuth's boundary tags, in 1968, copy each block's size into its last word too, so the block before is one step away.
f05926f0492b.zh: 这是经典的设计。<bookmark mark='a'/>堆是一段被切成块的内存，每块开头有一个小小的头部，记着它的大小和是否在用。<bookmark mark='b'/>空闲块被串成一个链表。<bookmark mark='c'/>要分配，就沿着链表找一个足够大的块，交出它的前一部分，剩下的留在链表里。<bookmark mark='d'/>要释放，就把块标成空闲，如果邻居也空闲，就把它们合并成一个更大的块，免得堆碎成太小而用不上的碎片。<bookmark mark='e'/>找后一个邻居很容易，因为它的头部紧跟着我们。找前一个才是巧妙之处：高德纳1968 年的边界标签，把每个块的大小在它的最后一个字里也复制一份，于是前一个块一步就能找到。

09009791c3a3.en: To compare allocators honestly we need real requests, not made-up ones. <bookmark mark='a'/> So we recorded a real program: Perl, counting the words of Pride and Prejudice, which builds a hash table much like the one Part 17 will build. We wrote our own malloc that logs every request and then calls the real one, and slipped it in front of the C library, a trick chapter eleven explains. <bookmark mark='b'/> Over a hundred and forty thousand allocations, and most of them tiny: sixteen bytes or less, the size of a short word and its bookkeeping. <bookmark mark='c'/> And the live data climbs as the table fills, to about two megabytes. <bookmark mark='d'/> Now we can replay this exact sequence through allocators of our own.
09009791c3a3.zh: 要公平地比较分配器，我们需要真实的请求，而不是编出来的。<bookmark mark='a'/>所以我们记录了一个真实的程序：Perl 数《傲慢与偏见》里的词，它建的哈希表和第17部分要搭的很像。我们写了自己的 malloc，记下每一个请求再调用真正的那个，并把它塞到 C 库前面，第十一章会解释这个技巧。<bookmark mark='b'/>十四万多次分配，大多数都很小：十六字节或更少，一个短词加上它的簿记那么大。<bookmark mark='c'/>随着表被填满，活着的数据一路攀升，到大约两兆字节。<bookmark mark='d'/>现在我们可以把这个序列原样重放给我们自己的分配器。

e8315b0c7561.en: Chapter seven. Five allocators, one real trace.
e8315b0c7561.zh: 第七章。五个分配器，一条真实轨迹。

d20a20e48bbf.en: When several free blocks would do, which should a request get? <bookmark mark='a'/> First fit takes the first one it finds, in address order. Next fit does the same but starts each search where the last one stopped, so it does not keep re-scanning the front. Best fit takes the smallest block that fits, leaving the biggest pieces intact. Segregated fits keeps a separate list for each size class and looks in the request's own class first. And the buddy system allows only blocks whose sizes are powers of two, which makes splitting and merging almost free. <bookmark mark='b'/> We implemented all five on the same simulated heap and replayed Perl's trace through each.
d20a20e48bbf.zh: 当好几个空闲块都可以时，一个请求该给哪一个？<bookmark mark='a'/>首次适配按地址顺序取它找到的第一个。下次适配做法一样，但每次搜索都从上次停下的地方开始，免得一遍遍重扫前面。最佳适配取能放下的最小的块，让最大的块保持完整。分离适配为每个大小类别各留一个链表，先在请求自己的类别里找。伙伴系统只允许大小为二的幂的块，这让切分和合并几乎不花代价。<bookmark mark='b'/>我们在同一个模拟的堆上实现了全部五种，把 Perl 的轨迹逐一重放给它们。

c1d7dc33e4af.en: Here are the results. <bookmark mark='a'/> The measure is fragmentation: the heap each allocator needed, divided by the most bytes the program ever had live at once. One would be perfect. <bookmark mark='b'/> First fit, best fit and segregated fits all land at about one point one three: thirteen percent overhead, most of it headers and rounding on Perl's tiny blocks, not wasted holes. Next fit is a little worse. The buddy system needs nearly eighty percent more, because rounding every request up to a power of two wastes a quarter of each block on average. <bookmark mark='c'/> Speed is a different story. Next fit, meant to be fast, examines seventeen blocks per request on this trace; segregated fits examines fewer than one, because the right list is usually non-empty at its head. <bookmark mark='d'/> That combination, little waste and almost no searching, is why real allocators are built on size classes.
c1d7dc33e4af.zh: 结果在这里。<bookmark mark='a'/>衡量标准是碎片率：每个分配器需要的堆，除以程序同时活着的字节数的最大值。一就是完美。<bookmark mark='b'/>首次适配、最佳适配和分离适配都落在一点一三左右：百分之十三的开销，大多是 Perl 那些小块上的头部和取整，而不是浪费掉的空洞。下次适配稍差一点。伙伴系统要多出将近百分之八十，因为把每个请求都取整到二的幂，平均浪费每个块的四分之一。<bookmark mark='c'/>速度是另一回事。本该很快的下次适配，在这条轨迹上每个请求要查看十七个块；分离适配不到一个，因为对的那个链表通常在表头就有块。<bookmark mark='d'/>浪费少、几乎不用搜索，这种组合正是真实分配器都建立在大小类别上的原因。

fd312b3f274e.en: The buddy system, from Kenneth Knowlton in 1965, trades space for simplicity. <bookmark mark='a'/> Every block is a power of two. A request for thirty bytes splits a block in half, and in half again, until a thirty-two-byte block fits. <bookmark mark='b'/> Each half's partner, its buddy, sits at its own address with one bit flipped, the bit of the block's size, so a single exclusive-or finds it. <bookmark mark='c'/> When a block is freed and its buddy is free too, the two merge into their parent, and the check repeats one level up. <bookmark mark='d'/> All of this is fast. The cost is rounding: a request of thirty-three bytes gets sixty-four. Waste inside a block is internal fragmentation; waste between blocks, which first fit suffers from, is external.
fd312b3f274e.zh: 伙伴系统，肯尼思·诺尔顿 1965 年提出，用空间换简单。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个块都是二的幂。一个三十字节的请求把一个块劈成两半，再劈成两半，直到一个三十二字节的块正好放下。<bookmark mark='b'/>每一半的伙伴就在它自己的地址翻转一位的地方，翻的是块大小那一位，所以一次异或就能找到。<bookmark mark='c'/>一个块被释放而它的伙伴也空闲时，两者合并成它们的父块，并在上一层重复这个检查。<bookmark mark='d'/>这一切都很快。代价是取整：一个三十三字节的请求会得到六十四。块内部的浪费叫内部碎片；块之间的浪费，也就是首次适配受的苦，叫外部碎片。

44f27d5090d4.en: Real allocators combine these ideas. <bookmark mark='a'/> The C library on this machine uses ptmalloc, descended from Doug Lea's allocator: bins of free blocks by size, boundary tags and coalescing. <bookmark mark='b'/> Newer allocators, jemalloc, tcmalloc and mimalloc, carve pages into blocks of one size class each and give every thread its own cache of free blocks. <bookmark mark='c'/> Very large requests skip the heap entirely and get fresh pages from the operating system, which is Part 32's subject. <bookmark mark='d'/> The per-thread caches are Part 10's lesson again: a single shared free list would be a cache line every core fights over. <bookmark mark='e'/> And in languages with garbage collection, the runtime decides when to free, which Part 15 builds.
44f27d5090d4.zh: 真实的分配器把这些想法组合起来。<bookmark mark='a'/>这台机器上的 C 库用的是 ptmalloc，它源自道格·利的分配器：按大小分的空闲块箱、边界标签和合并。<bookmark mark='b'/>更新的分配器，jemalloc、tcmalloc 和 mimalloc，把页切成同一大小类别的块，并给每个线程一个自己的空闲块缓存。<bookmark mark='c'/>非常大的请求干脆绕过堆，直接从操作系统拿新的页，那是第32部分的主题。<bookmark mark='d'/>每线程缓存又是第10部分的教训：一个共享的空闲链表会是每个核都在争抢的缓存行。<bookmark mark='e'/>在有垃圾回收的语言里，由运行时决定何时释放，第15部分会搭建它。

ff570514bada.en: Chapter eight. Knuth's rule and Robson's bound.
ff570514bada.zh: 第八章。克努特法则与罗布森界。

692a356d7cd4.en: How many holes does a heap have? Knuth found a law, in 1968. <bookmark mark='a'/> In a heap that has settled into equilibrium, with N blocks in use, there are about one half p times N free holes, where p is the chance that an allocation does not use up its hole exactly. Since p is usually near one, about half as many holes as blocks. The proof is a counting argument. <bookmark mark='b'/> Classify the blocks in use by how many of their two neighbours are free: none, one, or two. <bookmark mark='c'/> Each hole sits between two blocks in use, because neighbouring holes would have been merged, so twice the number of holes equals B plus two C. <bookmark mark='d'/> Now ask how holes come and go. Freeing an A-block makes a new hole; freeing a C-block merges two holes and its own space into one; freeing a B-block just extends a hole. <bookmark mark='e'/> And an allocation removes a hole only when it uses it up exactly. <bookmark mark='f'/> In equilibrium the gains and losses balance, which says A minus C equals one minus p, times N. Substitute, and the holes come to one half p N.
692a356d7cd4.zh: 一个堆里有多少个空洞？高德纳在 1968 年找到了一条定律。<bookmark mark='a'/>在一个已经稳定到平衡态的堆里，有 N 个块在用，大约就有二分之一 p 乘 N 个空闲空洞，其中 p 是一次分配没有恰好用完它的空洞的概率。由于 p 通常接近一，空洞数大约是块数的一半。证明是一个计数论证。<bookmark mark='b'/>按两个邻居中有几个是空闲的，把在用的块分成三类：零个、一个、两个。<bookmark mark='c'/>每个空洞都夹在两个在用的块之间，因为相邻的空洞早就被合并了，所以空洞数的两倍等于 B 加两倍的 C。<bookmark mark='d'/>现在问空洞怎样产生又怎样消失。释放一个 A 块产生一个新空洞；释放一个 C 块把两个空洞和它自己的空间合成一个；释放一个 B 块只是让一个空洞变大。<bookmark mark='e'/>而一次分配只有恰好用完一个空洞时才会消掉它。<bookmark mark='f'/>在平衡态里得失相抵，这说明 A 减 C 等于一减 p 乘 N。代进去，空洞数就是二分之一 p N。

1ae7260aebbf.en: We checked it. <bookmark mark='a'/> A first-fit heap with two hundred, a thousand and three thousand blocks in use; at every step a random block is freed and a new one of random size allocated. We count the holes, and measure p by counting how often an allocation split its hole rather than using it up. <bookmark mark='b'/> Holes per block, against one half of p: point four three eight against point four three five; point three nine nine against point four oh one; point three eight three against point three eight three. The rule is exact enough to plan with.
1ae7260aebbf.zh: 我们检验了它。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个首次适配的堆，分别有两百、一千和三千个块在用；每一步随机释放一个块，再分配一个随机大小的新块。我们数空洞，并通过统计分配切开空洞而不是用完它的频率来测量 p。<bookmark mark='b'/>每块的空洞数，对比二分之一 p：零点四三八对零点四三五；零点三九九对零点四零一；零点三八三对零点三八三。这条法则精确到可以拿来做规划。

497ce696aff2.en: Knuth's rule describes the average heap. What about the worst? <bookmark mark='a'/> In 1971 and 1974 John Robson proved a sharp answer. If a program never has more than M bytes live, and no block bigger than n units, then for every allocator there is a program that forces it to use about M times one half log two n, plus one. <bookmark mark='b'/> The program is an adversary that watches where the allocator puts things. It fills memory with small blocks, then frees half of them, choosing which so that every hole is too small for the next, larger size. It doubles the size, and repeats. Each phase forces the allocator to take about M over two of fresh memory. <bookmark mark='c'/> We ran this adversary against our first-fit heap. The heap grows by half of M at each doubling, and the dots fall exactly on Robson's curve: four and a half M for blocks up to four kilobytes. <bookmark mark='d'/> The bound holds for any allocator that never moves a block. The only escape is to move them, compacting the heap, which needs to know where every pointer is: a garbage collector, Part 15.
497ce696aff2.zh: 克努特法则描述的是平均的堆。最坏的呢？<bookmark mark='a'/>1971 年和 1974 年，约翰·罗布森证明了一个锐利的答案。如果一个程序活着的数据从不超过 M 字节，且没有块大于 n 个单位，那么对每一个分配器，都存在一个程序迫使它用上大约 M 乘以二分之一 log₂ n 再加一。<bookmark mark='b'/>这个程序是一个对手，它盯着分配器把东西放在哪里。它先用小块填满内存，再释放其中一半，挑选释放哪些，使得每个空洞都放不下下一个更大的尺寸。它把尺寸翻倍，重复。每一阶段都迫使分配器再拿大约 M 的一半的新内存。<bookmark mark='c'/>我们让这个对手对付我们的首次适配堆。尺寸每翻一倍，堆就长 M 的一半，那些点恰好落在罗布森的曲线上：块到四千字节时是四点五 M。<bookmark mark='d'/>这个界对任何从不移动块的分配器都成立。唯一的出路是移动它们、压实堆，而这需要知道每个指针在哪里：垃圾回收器，第15部分。

67735cb783f6.en: Now the same story on a real machine. <bookmark mark='a'/> Two C files. main uses a function, count, and a variable, total, that live in the other file, and it has data of its own: a pointer to a string, and a counter private to the file. <bookmark mark='b'/> lib defines count and total, and one weak variable we will come back to. <bookmark mark='c'/> Each file is compiled on its own into an object file, and then the two are linked into a program. We compiled them on this computer and read the object files with the standard tool, readelf.
67735cb783f6.zh: 现在在一台真实的机器上把这个故事再讲一遍。<bookmark mark='a'/>两个 C 文件。main 用到一个函数 count 和一个变量 total，它们住在另一个文件里；它也有自己的数据：一个指向字符串的指针，和一个文件私有的计数器。<bookmark mark='b'/>lib 定义了 count 和 total，还有一个弱变量，我们待会儿再说它。<bookmark mark='c'/>每个文件单独编译成一个目标文件，然后两者链接成一个程序。我们在这台计算机上编译它们，并用标准工具 readelf 读这些目标文件。

bde0122df2ab.en: An object file is a set of named sections. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here are main dot o's. The machine code is in one section, the string constants in a read-only one. The pointer greeting gets a section of its own, because its value, the address of the string, is not known yet. The private counter goes in bss: a section that records only its size, since it starts as zeros and needs no space in the file. Then two sections of relocations, the holes and what fills them, and the symbol table with its names. <bookmark mark='b'/> The format is ELF, from AT and T's System V in 1988, used today by Linux, the BSDs and most game consoles. Pebble's object files are a toy version of it.
bde0122df2ab.zh: 目标文件是一组有名字的节。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是 main.o 的。机器码在一个节里，字符串常量在一个只读节里。指针 greeting 有自己的一个节，因为它的值，也就是那个字符串的地址，现在还不知道。私有的计数器放进 bss：这个节只记下大小，因为它从全零开始，在文件里不占空间。然后是两个重定位节，也就是那些洞和填洞的东西，还有带着名字的符号表。<bookmark mark='b'/>这种格式叫 ELF，出自 1988 年美国电话电报公司的 System V，今天 Linux、各个 BSD 和大多数游戏机都在用。Pebble 的目标文件是它的一个玩具版。

83a7e54bfd5e.en: The symbol table says what each file offers and what it needs. <bookmark mark='a'/> main dot o defines main and greeting as global symbols, visible to other files, and the counter as local. It lists total, count and the C library's printf as undefined: used here, defined elsewhere. lib dot o defines count and total, globally, and verbose as weak. And it needs strlen: the optimizer recognised count's loop as a string length and replaced it with a call to the library. <bookmark mark='b'/> The relocations say exactly which bytes depend on which symbol, and how: here, a 32-bit distance from the instruction to the target, a call that may go through a table we meet in chapter eleven, or a whole 64-bit address for the pointer.
83a7e54bfd5e.zh: 符号表说明每个文件提供什么、需要什么。<bookmark mark='a'/>main.o 把 main 和 greeting 定义为全局符号，其他文件看得见；计数器则是局部的。它把 total、count 和 C 库的 printf 列为未定义：这里用到，别处定义。lib.o 全局地定义了 count 和 total，并把 verbose 定义为弱符号。它还需要 strlen：优化器认出 count 的循环是在求字符串长度，就把它换成了一次库调用。<bookmark mark='b'/>重定位精确地说明哪些字节依赖哪个符号、以什么方式依赖：这里有从指令到目标的 32 位距离，有可能经过一张表的调用，那张表我们在第十一章会见到，还有给指针用的完整 64 位地址。

45d9b33c742a.en: From these tables the linker applies a few rules. <bookmark mark='a'/> Every symbol some file needs must be defined somewhere. <bookmark mark='b'/> Two strong definitions of one name are an error. <bookmark mark='c'/> A strong definition beats any number of weak ones, <bookmark mark='d'/> and if there are only weak ones, one is chosen. <bookmark mark='e'/> Leave out lib dot o and this machine's linker reports the undefined references; include it twice and it reports a multiple definition. Weak symbols exist so that a library can provide a default that a program may override, like a default error handler, or even malloc itself.
45d9b33c742a.zh: 根据这些表，链接器执行几条规则。<bookmark mark='a'/>某个文件需要的每个符号，都必须在某处有定义。<bookmark mark='b'/>同一个名字有两个强定义，是错误。<bookmark mark='c'/>一个强定义胜过任意多个弱定义，<bookmark mark='d'/>如果只有弱定义，就挑其中一个。<bookmark mark='e'/>去掉 lib.o，这台机器的链接器就报告未定义的引用；把它放进去两次，就报告重复定义。弱符号的存在，是为了让库可以提供一个程序能覆盖的默认实现，比如默认的错误处理函数，甚至 malloc 本身。

01741d3bce89.en: Chapter ten. Linking, step by step.
01741d3bce89.zh: 第十章。一步一步地链接。

614e4fa3bfbd.en: Now our own linker, on the Job's four object files. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each file says what it defines and what it needs. main defines start and needs getc, lookup and report. The table defines lookup and report and needs alloc, putc and printnum. alloc and io need nothing. <bookmark mark='b'/> The first job is to match every need to exactly one definition. Here, every name is defined once, so each gets an address. <bookmark mark='c'/> Leave out the allocator, or include it twice, and Pebble's linker refuses, with the same two complaints this machine's linker gave.
614e4fa3bfbd.zh: 现在用我们自己的链接器，处理任务的四个目标文件。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个文件都说明自己定义了什么、需要什么。main 定义了 start，需要 getc、lookup 和 report。表定义了 lookup 和 report，需要 alloc、putc 和 printnum。alloc 和 io 什么都不需要。<bookmark mark='b'/>第一件事是把每个需求和恰好一个定义配上对。这里每个名字都只定义了一次，所以每个都得到一个地址。<bookmark mark='c'/>漏掉分配器，或者把它放进去两次，Pebble 的链接器就会拒绝，抱怨的和这台机器的链接器一模一样。

fa9d71300b97.en: Step two: decide where everything goes. <bookmark mark='a'/> The linker lays out all the files' code first, one after another in the order the files were given, each aligned to sixteen bytes. Then all their data. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then the bss sections, which take addresses but no bytes in the file: here, the allocator's three hundred and eighty-four kilobytes of heap. <bookmark mark='c'/> So the program file is eight hundred and sixty-four bytes, but the program in memory is almost four hundred kilobytes. Now that every section has an address, so does every symbol.
fa9d71300b97.zh: 第二步：决定每样东西放在哪里。<bookmark mark='a'/>链接器先摆放所有文件的代码，按给出文件的顺序一个接一个，每段按十六字节对齐。然后是它们全部的数据。<bookmark mark='b'/>再然后是 bss 节，它们占地址，但在文件里不占字节：这里是分配器那三百八十四千字节的堆。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以程序文件只有八百六十四个字节，内存里的程序却将近四百千字节。既然每个节都有了地址，每个符号也就有了。

204d1339df7f.en: Step three: fill the holes. <bookmark mark='a'/> There are 16 relocations across the four files. Each says where the hole is, what kind of hole, and which symbol's address belongs in it. <bookmark mark='b'/> Take one: the table code loads the address of its list head with la, which the assembler emitted as a lui and an ori with zeros. head now lives at 832. The linker splits that into its top twenty-two bits, 0, and its low ten, 832, and writes them into the two instructions. <bookmark mark='c'/> For a call, it writes the distance from the call to the function, counted in instructions, into the jump's 22-bit field. <bookmark mark='d'/> That is all a static linker does. Load the result and run it, and the four files behave as one program.
204d1339df7f.zh: 第三步：把洞填上。<bookmark mark='a'/>四个文件里一共有16条重定位。每一条说明洞在哪里、是哪种洞、该填进哪个符号的地址。<bookmark mark='b'/>拿一条来看：表的代码用 la 载入它链表头的地址，汇编器把它发成一条 lui 加一条 ori，立即数都是零。head 现在住在 832。链接器把它拆成高二十二位0和低十位832，写进这两条指令。<bookmark mark='c'/>对一次调用，它把从调用处到函数的距离，以指令条数计，写进跳转的 22 位字段。<bookmark mark='d'/>静态链接器做的就是这些。把结果装载起来运行，四个文件就表现得像一个程序。

549c01427aa2.en: Real programs also link against libraries, and a static library is simply an archive of object files. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is one we built, lib job dot a, holding two members: count dot o, and unused dot o, which carries a hundred-kilobyte table. <bookmark mark='b'/> The linker reads its inputs left to right, keeping a list of the names still undefined. After main dot o, that list holds count. <bookmark mark='c'/> In the archive it takes only the members that define a name on the list: count dot o comes in, unused dot o stays out. The program is 16 kilobytes; listing all three object files instead gives 112. <bookmark mark='d'/> Now put the library first. When the linker reads it, nothing is undefined yet, so it takes nothing; then main dot o needs count, too late. Undefined reference to count. <bookmark mark='e'/> That is why, on a command line, libraries go after the files that use them.
549c01427aa2.zh: 真实的程序还要链接库，而静态库不过是目标文件的一个归档。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是我们建的一个，libjob.a，里面有两个成员：count.o，以及带着一张十万字节表格的 unused.o。<bookmark mark='b'/>链接器从左到右读它的输入，并记着一份仍未定义的名字清单。读完 main.o，清单里有 count。<bookmark mark='c'/>在归档里，它只取那些能定义清单上某个名字的成员：count.o 进来了，unused.o 留在外面。程序是16千字节；改为直接列出全部三个目标文件，则是112千字节。<bookmark mark='d'/>现在把库放在前面。链接器读到它时，还没有任何未定义的名字，所以它什么也不取；然后 main.o 需要 count，已经晚了。未定义的引用：count。<bookmark mark='e'/>这就是为什么在命令行上，库要放在用到它的文件之后。

0e1910dc6a3b.en: A two-line program that prints hello, linked two ways on this computer. <bookmark mark='a'/> Linked statically, the parts of the C library it uses are copied into the file: 767 kilobytes. Linked dynamically, the file is 16 kilobytes, <bookmark mark='b'/> because it holds only a note that it needs the C library, and a list of the functions it will take from it: here, just puts, with a version tag saying which interface of glibc it expects. <bookmark mark='c'/> The price is a little start-up work, finding and mapping the library, about a tenth of a millisecond here. <bookmark mark='d'/> The gains are large: one copy of the library in memory, shared by every process that uses it, and a security fix to the library fixes every program at once. ldd lists what a program will load.
0e1910dc6a3b.zh: 一个打印 hello 的两行程序，在这台计算机上用两种方式链接。<bookmark mark='a'/>静态链接时，它用到的那部分 C 库被复制进文件：767千字节。动态链接时，文件只有16千字节，<bookmark mark='b'/>因为它只装着一张条子，说它需要 C 库，外加一份它要从库里取的函数清单：这里只有 puts，带一个版本标签，说明它期望 glibc 的哪一版接口。<bookmark mark='c'/>代价是一点启动工作，找到并映射这个库，在这里大约十分之一毫秒。<bookmark mark='d'/>好处很大：内存里只有一份库，被每个用它的进程共享；修复库里的一个安全漏洞，就同时修好了每一个程序。ldd 会列出一个程序要装载什么。

415b43c2ebc3.en: How does a call reach a library whose address is not known until the program runs? <bookmark mark='a'/> A shared library is loaded at a different address in different processes, so its code cannot contain absolute addresses. It is compiled as position-independent code: every address it needs is kept in a table of data, the global offset table, which the loader fills in. <bookmark mark='b'/> Calls into another library go through a small stub in the procedure linkage table, which jumps to whatever the table holds. <bookmark mark='c'/> On the first call the table points back into the dynamic linker, which looks the function up, writes its real address into the table, <bookmark mark='d'/> and jumps there. Every later call goes through the stub straight to the function. This is lazy binding, and it is the reason for the PLT32 relocation we saw on count.
415b43c2ebc3.zh: 一次调用怎样到达一个直到程序运行才知道地址的库？<bookmark mark='a'/>共享库在不同的进程里装载在不同的地址，所以它的代码里不能有绝对地址。它被编译成位置无关代码：它需要的每个地址都放在一张数据表里，叫全局偏移表，由装载器填写。<bookmark mark='b'/>调用另一个库要经过过程链接表里的一个小桩，它跳到表里存着的地方。<bookmark mark='c'/>第一次调用时，表指回动态链接器，后者查到这个函数，把它的真实地址写进表里，<bookmark mark='d'/>然后跳过去。以后的每次调用都经过桩直达函数。这叫惰性绑定，也正是我们在 count 上看到 PLT32 重定位的原因。

d3e9311b86a8.en: Dynamic linking has a remarkable side effect: you can replace a library function without touching the program. <bookmark mark='a'/> Set LD_PRELOAD to a library of your own, and the dynamic linker searches it before the C library. <bookmark mark='b'/> So when Perl calls malloc, it reaches our malloc, which writes a record of the request and then calls the real one, found by asking for the next definition of the same name. <bookmark mark='c'/> That is how chapter six recorded almost two hundred and seventy-seven thousand events from an unmodified Perl. <bookmark mark='d'/> Profilers and memory-leak checkers use the same trick, and so, sometimes, does malware.
d3e9311b86a8.zh: 动态链接有一个了不起的副作用：你可以不碰程序就替换一个库函数。<bookmark mark='a'/>把 LD_PRELOAD 设成你自己的一个库，动态链接器就会先在它里面找，再找 C 库。<bookmark mark='b'/>于是 Perl 调用 malloc 时，到达的是我们的 malloc，它记下这个请求，再调用真正的那个，后者是通过请求同名的下一个定义找到的。<bookmark mark='c'/>第六章就是这样从一个没改过的 Perl 里记下将近二十七万七千个事件的。<bookmark mark='d'/>性能分析器和内存泄漏检查器用的是同一个技巧，有时恶意软件也是。

9d311d66588c.en: Chapter twelve. Loading and the address space.
9d311d66588c.zh: 第十二章。装载与地址空间。

69e76da3748f.en: Here is a real process on this computer, as Linux describes it in the file proc self maps. <bookmark mark='a'/> At the bottom, the program itself: its constants, its code, its data. Above them the heap, which grows upward as malloc asks for more. Far above, the C library and the dynamic linker, mapped into the space. And at the top, the stack, which grows downward. The gaps between are vast, terabytes of addresses that are simply not mapped. <bookmark mark='b'/> Each region has its own permissions. Code may be executed but not written. Data and the stack may be written, but not executed, which will matter in chapter fourteen.
69e76da3748f.zh: 这是这台计算机上的一个真实进程，按 Linux 在 /proc/self/maps 文件里的描述。<bookmark mark='a'/>最底下是程序本身：它的常量、代码和数据。它们上面是堆，随着 malloc 要更多内存而向上长。远在上方，是映射进这个空间的 C 库和动态链接器。最顶上是栈，它向下长。中间的空隙大得惊人，数以太字节计的地址根本没有映射。<bookmark mark='b'/>每个区域都有自己的权限。代码可以执行但不能写。数据和栈可以写但不能执行，这一点在第十四章会很要紧。

ad2fcbf0e36b.en: Run a program that prints where things are, three times. <bookmark mark='a'/> The address of main, of a global variable, of a heap block, of a local variable on the stack, and of the C library's printf. Every run, every one is different. <bookmark mark='b'/> This is address-space layout randomization. It was introduced by the PaX project in 2001 and is on by default everywhere now. Its point is security: an attack that needs to know where something is, like the one in chapter fourteen, has to guess. <bookmark mark='c'/> Switch it off, and the stack is at the same address every time.
ad2fcbf0e36b.zh: 运行一个打印各样东西位置的程序，运行三次。<bookmark mark='a'/>main 的地址、一个全局变量的地址、一个堆块的地址、栈上一个局部变量的地址，以及 C 库 printf 的地址。每次运行，每一个都不同。<bookmark mark='b'/>这就是地址空间布局随机化。它由 PaX 项目在 2001 年引入，如今到处都默认开启。它的意义在于安全：一个需要知道某样东西在哪里的攻击，比如第十四章那个，就只能去猜。<bookmark mark='c'/>把它关掉，栈每次都在同一个地址。

5fe141ce8a1b.en: Last, how does main get its arguments? <bookmark mark='a'/> When you type job pride dot text, the operating system's loader copies the strings to the very top of the new process's stack, then below them an array of pointers to the strings, ending in a null, and below that their count. <bookmark mark='b'/> The first code to run is not main but a small routine called start, which finds those values and calls main with them. <bookmark mark='c'/> Pebble's loader, the last function in our linker, builds exactly this layout, and passes the count and the array in a0 and a1.
5fe141ce8a1b.zh: 最后，main 怎样拿到它的参数？<bookmark mark='a'/>当你键入 job pride.txt，操作系统的装载器把这些字符串复制到新进程栈的最顶端，在它们下面放一个指向这些字符串的指针数组，以空指针结尾，再下面是它们的个数。<bookmark mark='b'/>第一段运行的代码不是 main，而是一个叫 start 的小例程，它找到这些值，再拿它们调用 main。<bookmark mark='c'/>Pebble 的装载器，也就是我们链接器里的最后一个函数，建的正是这个布局，并把个数和数组放在 a0 和 a1 里传过去。

341013f8bfb8.en: C leaves some operations undefined. <bookmark mark='a'/> Overflowing a signed integer, reading past the end of an array, dereferencing a null pointer, using memory after freeing it. <bookmark mark='b'/> For these the standard does not say the program crashes, or gives a wrong answer. It says nothing at all: any behaviour is allowed. <bookmark mark='c'/> There were reasons. Machines handled overflow differently, and checking every array access costs time. <bookmark mark='d'/> But modern optimizers draw a sharper conclusion: since a correct program never does these things, the compiler may assume they never happen, and optimize on that assumption. We measured what that does on this computer.
341013f8bfb8.zh: C 把一些操作留作未定义。<bookmark mark='a'/>有符号整数溢出、读过数组的末尾、解引用空指针、释放之后还用那块内存。<bookmark mark='b'/>对这些，标准并不说程序会崩溃，或者给出错的答案。它什么也不说：任何行为都允许。<bookmark mark='c'/>这样做有它的理由。不同的机器处理溢出的方式不同，而检查每次数组访问要花时间。<bookmark mark='d'/>但现代的优化器得出了一个更尖锐的结论：既然正确的程序从不做这些事，编译器就可以假定它们永远不会发生，并按这个假定来优化。我们在这台计算机上测了这会带来什么。

0ce47dddcf84.en: First, signed overflow. <bookmark mark='a'/> A function asks whether x plus one is bigger than x. For the largest integer, x plus one overflows. <bookmark mark='b'/> On a real machine it wraps to the most negative number, so the honest answer is no. But gcc answers yes, one, because if overflow cannot happen, x plus one is always bigger, and it never computes anything. <bookmark mark='c'/> A loop that adds a billion to a positive counter until it goes negative ran three times without optimization and twice with it: the same source code, two behaviours. <bookmark mark='d'/> The flag f wrapv tells gcc that overflow wraps, and then both answers are the honest ones.
0ce47dddcf84.zh: 先看有符号溢出。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个函数问 x 加一是否大于 x。对最大的整数，x 加一会溢出。<bookmark mark='b'/>在真实的机器上，它绕回成最小的负数，所以诚实的答案是否。但 gcc 回答是，也就是一，因为如果溢出不可能发生，x 加一总是更大，它根本什么都不算。<bookmark mark='c'/>一个循环给一个正的计数器每次加十亿，直到它变成负数：不开优化跑了三圈，开了优化跑两圈。同样的源代码，两种行为。<bookmark mark='d'/>选项 -fwrapv 告诉 gcc 溢出会绕回，这时两个答案就都是诚实的了。

76f5ec1f4c09.en: Second, a null check. <bookmark mark='a'/> This function reads through a pointer, and only then checks whether the pointer was null. <bookmark mark='b'/> Without optimization, gcc compiles both: the load, the comparison, the early return. <bookmark mark='c'/> With optimization, the whole function is one load and a return. The reasoning: the program already dereferenced p, and dereferencing null is undefined, so p cannot be null, so the check can never fire. <bookmark mark='d'/> This is not hypothetical. In 2009 exactly this pattern in the Linux kernel's network tunnel driver let the compiler delete a null check, and the result was exploitable. Linux has been built ever since with a flag that forbids this particular optimization. The lesson of the chapter: in C, the program you meant and the program you wrote can differ, and the optimizer will take the one you wrote at its word.
76f5ec1f4c09.zh: 再看一次空指针检查。<bookmark mark='a'/>这个函数先通过一个指针读数，然后才检查这个指针是不是空的。<bookmark mark='b'/>不开优化，gcc 两样都编译出来：取数、比较、提前返回。<bookmark mark='c'/>开了优化，整个函数就是一次取数加一次返回。理由是：程序已经解引用了 p，而解引用空指针是未定义的，所以 p 不可能是空的，所以这个检查永远不会触发。<bookmark mark='d'/>这不是假想。2009 年，Linux 内核网络隧道驱动里恰好就是这个模式，让编译器删掉了一个空指针检查，结果可以被利用。从那以后，Linux 一直用一个禁止这种优化的选项来编译。这一章的教训是：在 C 里，你想写的程序和你写下的程序可能不一样，而优化器只认你写下的那个。

49f368995446.en: The practical defence is to catch undefined behaviour as it happens. <bookmark mark='a'/> Compile with the undefined-behaviour sanitizer, and our overflowing addition stops to report it: the largest int plus one cannot be represented in type int. <bookmark mark='b'/> AddressSanitizer catches memory errors: a write just past the end of a sixty-four-byte block from malloc, <bookmark mark='c'/> a read from a block already freed, <bookmark mark='d'/> and a write past an array on the stack, the very bug of the next chapter. Each report gives the address, the line of source, and for the heap, where the block was allocated.
49f368995446.zh: 实用的防御，是在未定义行为发生时就抓住它。<bookmark mark='a'/>用未定义行为检测器编译，我们那个溢出的加法就会停下来报告：最大的 int 加一，无法用 int 类型表示。<bookmark mark='b'/>AddressSanitizer 抓的是内存错误：在 malloc 给的一个六十四字节块的末尾之后写一个元素，<bookmark mark='c'/>从一个已经释放的块里读，<bookmark mark='d'/>以及越过栈上一个数组的末尾去写，正是下一章的那个错误。每份报告都给出地址、源代码的行号，对堆还会说明那个块是在哪里分配的。

d6327a0f5036.en: How does it know? <bookmark mark='a'/> AddressSanitizer surrounds every allocation with poisoned red zones, and holds freed blocks in quarantine for a while instead of handing them out again at once. <bookmark mark='b'/> It records which bytes may be touched in shadow memory: one shadow byte for every eight bytes of the program's, zero meaning all eight are fine. <bookmark mark='c'/> And the compiler puts a check of the shadow in front of every load and store the program makes. <bookmark mark='d'/> That costs. On this machine our word count of Pride and Prejudice took 2.0 times as long, and a loop that does nothing but malloc and free, 12 times. So sanitizers are switched on for testing and fuzzing, where Google's OSS-Fuzz has used them to find tens of thousands of bugs in open-source code, and switched off in production.
d6327a0f5036.zh: 它是怎么知道的？<bookmark mark='a'/>AddressSanitizer 在每次分配的周围加上有毒的红区，并且把释放的块在隔离区里放一阵子，而不是马上再分出去。<bookmark mark='b'/>它在影子内存里记下哪些字节可以碰：程序的每八个字节对应一个影子字节，零表示这八个字节都没问题。<bookmark mark='c'/>编译器在程序的每次取数和存数前面，都插入一次对影子的检查。<bookmark mark='d'/>这要付出代价。在这台机器上，我们统计《傲慢与偏见》词频的程序用了2.0倍的时间，而一个只做 malloc 和 free 的循环用了12倍。所以检测器在测试和模糊测试时打开，谷歌的 OSS-Fuzz 就用它们在开源代码里找到了数以万计的错误，而在生产环境中关掉。

a11d7153780c.en: Here is the greeting program from the start of this part, on Pebble. <bookmark mark='a'/> greet makes an eighty-byte frame. At the bottom, a sixty-four-byte buffer for the name; near the top, the saved return address, the way back to the caller. <bookmark mark='b'/> It passes the buffer to gets, which, like C's gets, copies input until it sees a newline, however long that is. <bookmark mark='c'/> The copy runs upward, from the bottom of the buffer towards the saved return address. So a name longer than seventy-six bytes reaches it.
a11d7153780c.zh: 这是本部分开头那个打招呼的程序，放在 Pebble 上。<bookmark mark='a'/>greet 建一个八十字节的栈帧。底部是装名字的六十四字节缓冲区；靠近顶部是保存的返回地址，回到调用者的路。<bookmark mark='b'/>它把缓冲区交给 gets，后者和 C 的 gets 一样，一直复制输入直到看见换行，不管有多长。<bookmark mark='c'/>复制是向上进行的，从缓冲区底部朝保存的返回地址去。所以一个长过七十六字节的名字就会碰到它。

7f5c96ffa221.en: So here is the attack. <bookmark mark='a'/> Its first part is code: 18 Pebble instructions that print the letters p w n e d and stop, 72 bytes. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then 4 bytes of padding, to fill the rest of the buffer and the gap: seventy-six bytes so far. <bookmark mark='c'/> Then four bytes that land exactly on the saved return address: the address of the buffer itself. <bookmark mark='d'/> gets copies all of it. greet prints its greeting, restores the return address from the stack, which is now ours, and returns, into the buffer, where our code runs. <bookmark mark='e'/> On the emulator it prints pwned. The attacker needed one fact, where the stack is, and on a machine with no randomization that never changes. This is how the Morris worm spread through the internet's fingerd servers in 1988, and Aleph One's 1996 article, Smashing the Stack for Fun and Profit, taught it to everyone.
7f5c96ffa221.zh: 攻击是这样的。<bookmark mark='a'/>它的第一部分是代码：18条 Pebble 指令，打印字母 p、w、n、e、d 然后停下，共72个字节。<bookmark mark='b'/>然后是4个字节的填充，填满缓冲区剩下的部分和那段空隙：到这里共七十六个字节。<bookmark mark='c'/>然后是恰好落在保存的返回地址上的四个字节：缓冲区自己的地址。<bookmark mark='d'/>gets 把它全部复制进去。greet 打印问候，从栈上恢复返回地址，而那个地址现在是我们的，然后返回，返回进了缓冲区，我们的代码就在那里运行。<bookmark mark='e'/>在模拟器上，它打印出 pwned。攻击者只需要知道一件事：栈在哪里；而在一台没有随机化的机器上，这永远不变。1988 年莫里斯蠕虫就是这样在互联网的 fingerd 服务器之间传播的，而 Aleph One 1996 年的文章《为了乐趣和利益粉碎栈》把它教给了所有人。

fabab913117b.en: Every program on this computer ships with defences against exactly this, and we built each one into Pebble. <bookmark mark='a'/> A stack canary: the function stores a secret word just below the return address, and checks it before returning. The overflow cannot reach the return address without trampling the canary, so the program stops with a report instead of jumping. <bookmark mark='b'/> A no-execute stack: the stack's pages may be written but not run, so jumping into the buffer faults. <bookmark mark='c'/> Randomization: the stack is somewhere new every run, so the attacker's address is a guess. <bookmark mark='d'/> And bounds on every pointer, which catch the very first byte out of bounds; that one is the Frontier chapter. <bookmark mark='e'/> None is perfect alone. Attackers answered the no-execute stack by stitching together fragments of code already in the program, return-oriented programming, which Part 55 takes up.
fabab913117b.zh: 这台计算机上的每个程序都带着针对这种攻击的防御，我们把每一种都做进了 Pebble。<bookmark mark='a'/>栈金丝雀：函数在返回地址下方存一个秘密的字，返回前检查它。溢出要碰到返回地址就必须踩坏金丝雀，于是程序报告错误并停下，而不是跳走。<bookmark mark='b'/>不可执行的栈：栈所在的页可以写，但不能运行，所以跳进缓冲区会出错。<bookmark mark='c'/>随机化：栈每次运行都在新的地方，所以攻击者的地址只是一个猜测。<bookmark mark='d'/>还有每个指针上的边界，它能在第一个越界的字节就抓住它；这是前沿一章的内容。<bookmark mark='e'/>没有哪一种单独就完美。攻击者对付不可执行栈的办法，是把程序里已有的代码片段缝合起来，也就是面向返回的编程，第55部分会讲它。

ee45dceb31ce.zh: 第十五章。链接起来的任务。

fe35489b6b32.en: Here is the Job written the way a compiler would write it. <bookmark mark='a'/> main reads letters into a buffer in its own stack frame. The table is a linked list of sixteen-byte nodes on the heap, kept in the order words were first seen, so ties break exactly as before. The allocator just bumps a pointer through three hundred and eighty-four kilobytes of bss, never freeing anything, which is all the Job needs. And the input and output routines include printnum, which keeps its digits in a small buffer in its frame. <bookmark mark='b'/> Each node holds a pointer to the next, a pointer to the word's letters, its length and its count. <bookmark mark='c'/> And every function obeys the calling convention of chapter four.
fe35489b6b32.zh: 这是按编译器的写法写出来的任务。<bookmark mark='a'/>main 把字母读进它自己栈帧里的一个缓冲区。表是堆上十六字节节点组成的链表，按单词第一次出现的次序排列，所以平局的打破方式和以前完全一样。分配器只是在 bss 的三百八十四千字节里往前推一个指针，从不释放任何东西，任务也只需要这些。输入输出例程里有 printnum，它把数字放在自己栈帧里的一个小缓冲区中。<bookmark mark='b'/>每个节点装着指向下一个节点的指针、指向单词字母的指针、它的长度和它的计数。<bookmark mark='c'/>每个函数都遵守第四章的调用约定。

8de67430d409.en: How does it compare with Part 6's single hand-written file? <bookmark mark='a'/> On a paragraph, the first chapter of Pride and Prejudice, and twenty thousand bytes, the output is identical every time. <bookmark mark='b'/> On the paragraph, version one is a few percent slower: every byte of input now costs a function call and return. <bookmark mark='c'/> On longer texts it is faster, by eleven percent at twenty thousand bytes, because following a next pointer takes one instruction fewer per entry than counting through an array. <bookmark mark='d'/> The stack never went deeper than three hundred and twenty bytes. <bookmark mark='e'/> Structure, it turns out, costs almost nothing here. But the algorithm has not changed: each word still pays for a scan of the vocabulary. Part 13's compiler will write this program automatically, and Act Four will change the algorithm.
8de67430d409.zh: 它和第6部分那个手写的单文件比怎么样？<bookmark mark='a'/>在一个段落、《傲慢与偏见》的第一章和两万字节上，输出每次都完全相同。<bookmark mark='b'/>在那个段落上，版本一慢了几个百分点：现在每个输入字节都要付出一次函数调用和返回。<bookmark mark='c'/>在更长的文本上它更快，两万字节时快百分之十一，因为顺着 next 指针走，每个表项比在数组里数过去少一条指令。<bookmark mark='d'/>栈从没深过三百二十个字节。<bookmark mark='e'/>原来结构在这里几乎不花什么。但算法没有变：每个词仍要为扫一遍词汇表付出代价。第13部分的编译器会自动写出这个程序，而第四幕会改变算法。

3330b630b3f5.en: The defences of chapter fourteen all work around the real problem: a pointer in C is just a number, and nothing knows how big the object behind it is. <bookmark mark='a'/> The CHERI project, from the University of Cambridge and SRI since 2010, changes the hardware so that a pointer is a capability: an address together with the bounds and permissions of the object, and a hidden tag bit that the program cannot forge. <bookmark mark='b'/> Every load and store is checked against the bounds of the pointer it uses, and a new pointer can only be made from an existing one, never larger. Arm built a prototype processor, Morello, in 2022. <bookmark mark='c'/> We added a miniature version to Pebble's emulator: when greet takes its buffer's address, the pointer gets bounds of sixty-four bytes, and the bounds travel with it. <bookmark mark='d'/> Run the attack again, and the machine traps on the sixty-fifth byte, before the return address is reached; an honest name is greeted as before.
3330b630b3f5.zh: 第十四章的那些防御，都是在绕开真正的问题：C 里的指针只是一个数，没有谁知道它背后的对象有多大。<bookmark mark='a'/>CHERI 项目，由剑桥大学和 SRI 从 2010 年开始，改造了硬件，让指针成为一种能力：一个地址，连同对象的边界和权限，外加一个程序无法伪造的隐藏标签位。<bookmark mark='b'/>每次取数和存数都要对照所用指针的边界检查，而新的指针只能从已有的指针造出来，而且永远不能变大。Arm 在 2022 年造出了原型处理器 Morello。<bookmark mark='c'/>我们在 Pebble 的模拟器里加了一个微缩版：greet 取它缓冲区的地址时，这个指针得到六十四字节的边界，边界随它一起走。<bookmark mark='d'/>再跑一遍攻击，机器在第六十五个字节上陷入，那时还没碰到返回地址；诚实的名字照常得到问候。

ba1fef00149b.en: The second frontier is meaning. <bookmark mark='a'/> To prove that a compiler is correct, you need a precise definition of what the source program means, undefined behaviour and all. <bookmark mark='b'/> Xavier Leroy's CompCert, begun in 2006, is a C compiler whose every pass is proved, in the Coq proof assistant, to preserve the meaning of every program that has no undefined behaviour; tests that find bugs in every other compiler have found none in its proved parts. <bookmark mark='c'/> The Cerberus project of Kayvan Memarian, Peter Sewell and colleagues built an executable semantics of C as programmers actually use it. <bookmark mark='d'/> The hardest question turned out to be pointer provenance: which object a pointer is allowed to reach, even when two pointers hold the same address. A model of it is now being standardized. <bookmark mark='e'/> Still open is a semantics that the standard, the optimizers and the billions of lines of existing code can all live with.
ba1fef00149b.zh: 第二个前沿是含义。<bookmark mark='a'/>要证明一个编译器是正确的，你需要给源程序的含义一个精确的定义，连同未定义行为。<bookmark mark='b'/>泽维尔·勒鲁瓦的 CompCert 始于 2006 年，是一个 C 编译器，它的每一遍都在 Coq 证明助手里被证明，对每个没有未定义行为的程序都保持其含义；那些在其他每个编译器里都找到错误的测试，在它被证明的部分里一个也没找到。<bookmark mark='c'/>卡万·梅马里安、彼得·休厄尔和同事们的 Cerberus 项目，为程序员实际使用的 C 建立了一套可执行的语义。<bookmark mark='d'/>结果最难的问题是指针来源：一个指针被允许到达哪个对象，即使两个指针装着同一个地址。它的一个模型正在被标准化。<bookmark mark='e'/>仍然悬而未决的，是一套标准、优化器和数十亿行现有代码都能接受的语义。

36b56929bff1.en: And the allocators of chapters six to eight have frontiers of their own. <bookmark mark='a'/> Robson's bound is achieved by a carefully designed allocator, but for the policies everyone uses, first fit and best fit, the exact worst case is still not known. <bookmark mark='b'/> Meanwhile real programs are nowhere near the worst case. Mark Johnstone and Paul Wilson measured real programs in 1998 and found that good policies waste only a few percent, as we saw with Perl. <bookmark mark='c'/> Why real programs are so kind has never been explained by a model. <bookmark mark='d'/> And allocators are now a security battleground: using memory after freeing it is among the commonest severe bugs in large C and C++ programs, and browsers now defend with quarantines that delay reuse, heaps segregated by type, and smart pointers like Chrome's MiraclePtr.
36b56929bff1.zh: 第六到第八章的分配器也有它们自己的前沿。<bookmark mark='a'/>罗布森界能被一个精心设计的分配器达到，但对大家都在用的策略，首次适配和最佳适配，确切的最坏情况至今未知。<bookmark mark='b'/>与此同时，真实的程序离最坏情况远得很。马克·约翰斯通和保罗·威尔逊 1998 年测量了真实的程序，发现好的策略只浪费百分之几，正如我们在 Perl 上看到的。<bookmark mark='c'/>真实程序为什么如此友好，从没有哪个模型解释过。<bookmark mark='d'/>而分配器如今是安全的战场：释放之后还使用内存，是大型 C 和 C++ 程序里最常见的严重错误之一，浏览器现在用延迟重用的隔离区、按类型分开的堆，以及像 Chrome 的 MiraclePtr 那样的智能指针来防御。

55ce528ee96c.en: What we built in this part. A program's life from source to process. Bytes, alignment and arrays, and control flow as branches and jump tables. The call stack, its frames, and the calling convention that lets separate functions cooperate. Five allocators run on a real program's hundred and forty-six thousand allocations, with Knuth's rule and Robson's bound confirmed by simulation. A linker and loader for Pebble, and the same machinery measured on this computer, through dynamic linking and a randomized address space. And what goes wrong: undefined behaviour, and the stack smash, with four defences.
55ce528ee96c.zh: 这一部分我们搭了什么。程序从源代码到进程的一生。字节、对齐和数组，以及作为分支和跳转表的控制流。调用栈、它的栈帧，以及让分别编写的函数能够合作的调用约定。五个分配器跑在一个真实程序的十四万六千次分配上，克努特法则和罗布森界都由模拟证实。Pebble 的链接器和装载器，以及在这台计算机上测量的同一套机制，经过动态链接和随机化的地址空间。还有会出的错：未定义行为，以及栈溢出攻击和四种防御。

0f7263ee9709.en: Where this comes back. The compiler that writes code like ours is Part 13. Garbage collectors, which can move objects and so escape Robson's bound, are Part 15. Exceptional control flow, signals and system calls are Part 31, and the pages behind the address space are Part 32. Proving programs and compilers correct is Part 54, and attacks that reuse a program's own code, and the question of whether you can trust your compiler at all, are Part 55.
0f7263ee9709.zh: 这些会在哪里再出现。写出我们这种代码的编译器是第13部分。能移动对象、从而摆脱罗布森界的垃圾回收器是第15部分。异常控制流、信号和系统调用是第31部分，地址空间背后的页是第32部分。证明程序和编译器正确是第54部分，而重用程序自身代码的攻击，以及你究竟能不能信任你的编译器这个问题，是第55部分。

300f5ac3f6b7.en: In practice. A debugger's backtrace is a walk up the stack's frames. AddressSanitizer, Valgrind and the undefined-behaviour sanitizer find the bugs of chapters thirteen and fourteen as they happen. Most build errors are linker errors: undefined references, duplicate symbols, libraries in the wrong order. Swapping the allocator is one of the cheapest performance wins in large servers. And stack protectors, no-execute pages, randomization and control-flow integrity are switched on by default by every mainstream toolchain.
300f5ac3f6b7.zh: 在实践中。调试器的回溯就是沿着栈帧往上走。AddressSanitizer、Valgrind 和未定义行为检测器会在第十三、十四章那些错误发生时就找到它们。大多数构建错误是链接错误：未定义的引用、重复的符号、顺序不对的库。在大型服务器上，换一个分配器是最便宜的性能收益之一。而栈保护、不可执行页、随机化和控制流完整性，每一个主流工具链都默认开启。

4e7f97a7fdc6.en: Six problems, with full solutions in the part's notes. Pause on any of them. The fifth is a build problem: write a real allocator in Pebble assembly and test it against the simulator on Perl's trace. The last, marked with a star, is a research problem: its answer is not known, and the notes say where to start.
4e7f97a7fdc6.zh: 六道习题，完整解答在本部分的笔记里。随时可以暂停。第五题是一道动手题：用 Pebble 汇编写一个真正的分配器，并在 Perl 的轨迹上拿它和模拟器对照。最后一道标着星号，是研究题：它的答案尚不知道，笔记里写了从哪里入手。

db0aab6bc010.en: Next time. To build Part 13's compiler we first need the theory of reading text: regular expressions, finite automata and grammars, and the parsers built from them. Part 12, Languages and Automata.
db0aab6bc010.zh: 下一次。要搭第13部分的编译器，我们先需要阅读文本的理论：正则表达式、有限自动机和文法，以及由它们构造的语法分析器。第12部分，语言与自动机。

9bd24692775d.en: The books and papers this part follows are on screen and in the notes. Thank you for watching.
9bd24692775d.zh: 这一部分依据的书和论文都在屏幕上和笔记里。感谢观看。
